classification: Post hoc descriptive activation and loss analysis of fixed independently audited DEVELOPMENT outcomes
method: Stream the fixed 730 candidate records only. Count actual receipt flags, compare eligible IDs to the saved baseline ID receipt and final compact hash to the immutable coverage-control hash. For the already reported lost groups, inspect saved target IDs, physical delivered bounds, initial protected matched-term unions and actual picks. No alternate ordering, utility, score or response is generated. Classifications are descriptive source-stage explanations, not new interventions.

interpretation: Every lost-group occurrence passed the prospective lexical term containment guard. Literal term preservation does not establish preservation of the requested behavior.
All four aspect_fill losses remove app.set from allocation across two distinct Express query units; duplicate hybrid rows are shared evidence, not independent failures.

Nine aspect_balanced losses remove previously eligible implementations; one consumes the old coverage/backfill opportunity for ExceptionMiddleware.__call__. Two retain the target but move it later so the 12000-character cap clips required evidence.

The two packing losses leave token headroom: Flask ends at line 1011 before the required 1012–1019 while using 11,991 characters / 3,544 tokens; urllib3 dense request ends at 465 before the required endpoint 513 while using 12,000 characters / 3,612 tokens.

Rare literal terms can be incidental: may selects res.download; boolean selects res.send/app.enabled; another selects an Emscripten worker module; complete/part/send select ASGI transport code. Adding stopwords would not by itself establish correct orchestration or behavior.
Both candidate conditions fail the frozen development qualification. Production defaults should remain unchanged and the fresh corpus should stay unobserved for this rejected study.
